## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `MooncakeConnector`, following the asymmetric P/D design in RFC #57383 and the full-prompt cache-hit replay design in RFC #57738.

P executes through the L20 pre-mix boundary and produces the transferable Main KV and Indexer K. D receives those regions, replays the bounded tail through the full target, and samples the first token.

## Implementation

This PR is intentionally split into two commits:

1. `13d89a71d0` - feature implementation and streamlined tests
   - Adds `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated Mooncake producer and consumer roles.
   - Adds the V4.1 execution boundary, explicit transfer profile, cache-only zero-token P completion, GPU completion event, request validation, and proxy `cache_only` handoff.
   - P runs L0-L19 plus the L20 pre-mix and canonical Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, then skips L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and DSpark.
   - D keeps bounded-replay state and DSpark state local. The validated D path supports DSpark K5 adaptive verification and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs.

2. `8d5b2b21c9` - Mooncake release-only pull fix
   - Bounded replay can discard a short remote hit while Mooncake still needs to release the producer blocks.
   - An empty pull has no local blocks and the consumer never enters `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. This commit releases the producer blocks without reporting a receive completion to the scheduler.

The current boundary is direct `MooncakeConnector`, NVIDIA, model runner V2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, SWA bounded replay with a 128-token window, the 40-layer V4.1-Flash topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling` and must not configure a speculator.

## Validation

### Latest-main rebase (2026-09-29)

Rebased onto `05d89636fc`. On macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, the focused model-boundary, cache-only, scheduler, config, and Mooncake tests passed (18 passed):

  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_dsv41_cache_only_prefill_finishes_without_sampling \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_transfers_global_groups_only \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_profile_rejects_missing_or_mixed_global_state \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py::test_cache_only_runner_waits_for_kv_writes_before_output \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_requires_bounded_replay \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py::test_dsv41_encoder_only_handoff_separates_producer_compile_hash \

```

`uvx ruff check` and `uvx ruff format --check` passed on all 21 changed Python files; `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. The upstream CUDA replay-batch suite could not be collected on this CPU-only machine because it allocates CUDA tensors at import time. The H20 serving and GSM8K measurements below were taken on the earlier nightly and have not been rerun on this rebased head.

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 8 NVIDIA H20 96 GB GPUs; one node for P and one for D
- Mooncake: 0.3.13.post1 over RDMA
- Baseline: the fixed nightly plus the release-only fix (tested with commit `50dcc87d1c`)
- Candidate: the same nightly with both PR commits

The baseline used conventional Mooncake P/D. Because D used DSpark K5, baseline P also used static DSpark K5 (`enable_adaptive_verification=false`) to keep the registered cache groups aligned. Candidate P did not load DSpark; candidate D used DSpark K5 adaptive verification. Decode used TP1 + DP8 + EP8 and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`. DeepEP was disabled: neither arm set `--all2all-backend`, and both selected the default `AgRsAll2AllManager` at runtime.

Thanks for this work, @wangyicong52. I tested a small extension on two H20 nodes (TP4 + EP on each side): **physically omit the unused decoder-layer weights on the encoder-only P**, rather than only skip their forward execution.

### What I changed

- Keep L0-L19 and the full L20 boundary layer. L20 is needed for the canonical Main-KV/Indexer-K writes.
- Replace L21-L39 with `PPMissingLayer` and skip only those layers' checkpoint tensors during loading. Preserve the original 40-layer model configuration and layer names. The full D is unchanged.
- This first experiment keeps the final norm and LM head allocated; it is not an attempt to prune every unused parameter. No checkpoint files were modified.

### Memory observations

The pruned P logs **38.14 GiB of model-loading GPU memory per TP rank**, compared with **73.55 GiB** for our previous full P. Available KV-cache memory per rank increased from **41.74 to 78.05 GiB** at the same GPU-memory-utilization setting.

Important qualification: that previous P also used DSpark K5 and a different source revision. The 35.41 GiB/rank reduction therefore **must not be attributed entirely to layer pruning**. Independently, the omitted L21-L39 tensors account for **130.779 GiB of checkpoint tensor payload in total**; that is checkpoint size, not a measured CUDA allocation reduction. A same-revision, unpruned encoder-only P control is still needed for an isolated savings claim.

### Correctness and one handoff issue

On PR head `a35de2b6530349600ca040620df2b68fc81f31c7`, I also encountered a block-alignment issue during the full P-to-D handoff: an 1815-token prompt leaves 29 blocks on P, but bounded replay imports 28 full 64-token blocks on D. The existing suffix selection then chooses P blocks 1-28 instead of 0-27. Transport succeeds, but a deterministic retrieval answer was incorrect. This suffix-selection assumption is already present in the PR's base; pruning does not change it.

A local, encoder-only-scoped fix clips P's transfer metadata to the scheduler-aligned import end before applying the existing suffix selection for D-local prefix hits. The CPU descriptor regression changes from 8/12 to 12/12 passing. With that fix, **12 short, sequential PD answer checks pass**, including cold/repeated hits, streaming, aligned/unaligned lengths, partial-prefix prewarm, and a shorter-than-one-block input. These checks use separate cache salts for local-D controls and cold PD requests. They are not a long-context, concurrency, or full quality evaluation.

Would you consider producer-only weight pruning as a follow-up to this PR? It looks useful for freeing additional KV capacity on P. I can share the small pruning/alignment diffs and focused regressions if helpful.

Following up with the two small local diffs, both tested against the current PR head `a35de2b6530349600ca040620df2b68fc81f31c7`. This investigation and the proposed code were AI-assisted; please treat these as patches for review, not an upstream-ready submission.

For a cold 1815-token request with 64-token blocks:

- P computes 29 blocks, including a partial tail.
- D's bounded replay imports 1792 tokens / 28 blocks.
- The existing `local_group[-n_remote:]` selects P blocks 1-28; it should select 0-27.
- With a 128-token D-local prefix hit, it selects 3-28 instead of 2-27.

The suffix selection itself predates this PR. I am reporting a concrete failure in this PR's new encoder-only path, **not claiming the PR introduced that line** or that every existing Mooncake request is affected. Simply replacing suffix selection with prefix selection would break partial local hits.

### 2. Producer-only decoder weight pruning (optional memory optimization)

With AgRs and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, my reading of the code is that a rank admitting a bounded-replay batch can make the target forward run eager across the DP group, while the replay tokens also add expert work and communication dependencies across ranks. Does this cause noticeable latency spikes for requests already decoding on other ranks?

The mean/P99 TPOT results are helpful, but request-level TPOT can average out isolated inter-token stalls over the 1024-token outputs. Do you have any per-token ITL distributions or timelines correlated with replay admission, or profiling that separates CUDA-graph fallback, MoE dispatch/combine wait, and expert compute? It would also be useful to know whether this interference differs from the conventional replay-enabled P/D baseline, especially during bursts of new requests.

@jiangkuaixue123 Thanks for pointing this out. Encoder-only prefill does have a measurable impact on decode performance (especially with DEP and FULL_DECODE_ONLY), and the P-side speedup does not always translate into an end-to-end improvement. Many thanks to @ivanium for running the additional GB200 benchmarks and helping clarify this tradeoff.

Both the baseline and candidate below include #59197. The baseline uses regular P/D, and the candidate enables encoder-only prefill.

**Hardware and workload**

- Two nodes, each with 4 GB200 GPUs.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, model runner V2, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graph mode, SWA bounded replay enabled, and no speculative decoding.
- Input length: 140,000 tokens, comprising one shared prefix of 131,600 tokens (94%) and an 8,400-token unique suffix.
- Decode test: 500 output tokens, concurrency 8/32/64/128, with the number of prompts equal to 8× concurrency.
- Prefill test: 1 output token, concurrency 1/4/16.
- The client sends token IDs with settings equivalent to `vllm bench serve`. Prefix caches are reset before each test point.

| DEP2 | 64 | 18.39 | 20.38 | +10.8% | -12.8% |
| DEP2 | 128 | 24.44 | 27.98 | +14.5% | -11.4% |
| DEP4 | 8 | 9.79 | 12.47 | +27.4% | -17.0% |
| DEP4 | 32 | 12.11 | 13.92 | +15.0% | -11.8% |
| DEP4 | 64 | 14.52 | 15.95 | +9.9% | -8.2% |
| DEP4 | 128 | 18.50 | 21.30 | +15.1% | -13.7% |

**Prefill: P-side processing time and end-to-end TTFT (ms)**

| Concurrency | P time, baseline | P time, candidate | Mean TTFT, baseline | Mean TTFT, candidate | Request throughput change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| 16 | 1309 | 727 (-44%) | 1923 | 2602 (+35%) | -27% |

The original motivation came partly from an issue in vLLM’s initial implementation: it replayed the SWA window on both P and D, even when P had already produced and transferred the required SWA state. Removing the P-side decoder computation therefore seemed like a natural optimization. #59197 subsequently fixed the redundant D-side replay for transfers carrying that state, leaving replay on the prefill side in that path. The tradeoff is now quite different: encoder-only prefill still needs D to reconstruct the missing state, so its additional impact on ongoing decode requests becomes much more important. I think encoder-only prefill still has value. First, it could reduce the weights loaded on P by omitting unused decoder layers. ## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `MooncakeConnector`, following the asymmetric P/D design in RFC #57383 and the full-prompt cache-hit replay design in RFC #57738.

P executes through the L20 pre-mix boundary and produces the transferable Main KV and Indexer K. D receives those regions, replays the bounded tail through the full target, and samples the first token.

## Implementation

This PR is intentionally split into two commits:

1. `13d89a71d0` - feature implementation and streamlined tests
   - Adds `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated Mooncake producer and consumer roles.
   - Adds the V4.1 execution boundary, explicit transfer profile, cache-only zero-token P completion, GPU completion event, request validation, and proxy `cache_only` handoff.
   - P runs L0-L19 plus the L20 pre-mix and canonical Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, then skips L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and DSpark.
   - D keeps bounded-replay state and DSpark state local. The validated D path supports DSpark K5 adaptive verification and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs.

2. `8d5b2b21c9` - Mooncake release-only pull fix
   - Bounded replay can discard a short remote hit while Mooncake still needs to release the producer blocks.
   - An empty pull has no local blocks and the consumer never enters `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. This commit releases the producer blocks without reporting a receive completion to the scheduler.

The current boundary is direct `MooncakeConnector`, NVIDIA, model runner V2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, SWA bounded replay with a 128-token window, the 40-layer V4.1-Flash topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling` and must not configure a speculator.

## Validation

### Latest-main rebase (2026-09-29)

The upstream CUDA replay-batch suite could not be collected on this CPU-only machine because it allocates CUDA tensors at import time. The H20 serving and GSM8K measurements below were taken on the earlier nightly and have not been rerun on this rebased head.

### Environment

- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a9eafde59cbd55182dc2265cc398b7186f0a0eaa`
- Hardware: two nodes, each with 8 NVIDIA H20 96 GB GPUs; one node for P and one for D
- Mooncake: 0.3.13.post1 over RDMA

The baseline used conventional Mooncake P/D. Because D used DSpark K5, baseline P also used static DSpark K5 (`enable_adaptive_verification=false`) to keep the registered cache groups aligned.
